description: Structured spec of a paper's design feature, emitted by the distiller node. Downstream integration agents implement against this document, so it must be complete enough to implement without the paper.

source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
source.citation: Toru Koizumi, Toshiki Maekawa, Masanari Mizuno, Maru Kuroki, Tomoaki Tsumura, and Ryota Shioya. 2025. RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables. In Proceedings of the 6th Championship Branch Prediction (CBP 2025), in conjunction with ISCA 2025, June 21, 2025, Tokyo, Japan, pp. 1-6.

summary: The `sr` feature is a register-value-aware statistical corrector (SC) component that captures correlations between recently computed register values and conditional branch directions without explicitly tracking dataflow dependencies. It tracks available register values using a 65-entry Tomasulo-like tracking table partitioned into 8 banks. For each register, a 12-bit digest is generated at execution/completion from integer, floating-point, or flag values and expires after 256 decoded instructions. At prediction time, per-bank usefulness tables (UT) determine the most useful valid register in each bank, whose digest is hashed with PC into three weight tables (WT). The resulting bank sums are scaled (by 2.5 if useful, else suppressed to 0) and accumulated into a component prediction sum sR that feeds the SC adder tree, providing substantial prediction accuracy gains especially right after branch mispredictions when execution pipelines flush and expose fresh register values.

state.name: Register Tracking Table (RTT)
state.organization: Direct-mapped array of 65 entries corresponding to 65 logical registers (R0..R64), split logically across 8 banks (Bank 0: 9 registers [R0, R8, ..., R64]; Banks 1..7: 8 registers each)
state.entry_format: valid: 1 bit, payload: 14 bits (holds either a 14-bit in-flight ROB tag or a 12-bit completed value digest right-justified), decay_ctr: 8 bits (saturating instruction countdown timer)
state.indexing: Directly indexed by logical register index (reg_id in 0..64)

state.name: Usefulness Tables (UT0, UT1, UT2)
state.organization: 3 tables per bank across 8 banks; each table contains 8 sets (entries). Each set stores a vector of 6-bit signed weights corresponding to all logical registers assigned to that bank (9 registers in Bank 0, 8 registers in Banks 1..7)
state.entry_format: Bank 0: 9 x 6-bit signed weights (54 bits per entry); Banks 1..7: 8 x 6-bit signed weights (48 bits per entry). Symmetrical 6-bit signed saturating counter [-32, 31] per register
state.indexing: Indexed by folded/skewed PC: hash(PC, table_id) % 8

state.name: Prediction Weight Table 0 (WT0)
state.organization: 8 banks, 512 entries per bank (4096 entries total across all banks)
state.indexing: Indexed by h0 = hash(PC, selected_reg_digest, bank_id) % 512

state.name: Prediction Weight Table 1 (WT1)
state.organization: 8 banks, 256 entries per bank (2048 entries total across all banks)
state.indexing: Indexed by h1 = hash(PC, selected_reg_digest, bank_id) % 256

state.name: Prediction Weight Table 2 (WT2)
state.organization: 8 banks, 128 entries per bank (1024 entries total across all banks)
state.indexing: Indexed by h2 = hash(PC, selected_reg_digest, bank_id) % 128

algorithms.name: generate_digest
algorithms.trigger: Execution / completion time of an instruction producing a register value
algorithms.notes: Handles integer, floating point, and condition-code registers. Per U3 and U4, leading/trailing counts saturate to 6 bits (0..63), and FP fields are shifted by 3 bits leaving digest[2:0] zeroed.

algorithms.name: track_register_decode
algorithms.notes: Invalidates previous valid digest and tracks pending in-flight producer via ROB tag.

algorithms.name: track_register_complete
algorithms.notes: Stores generated digest and marks register valid for branch prediction use.

algorithms.name: track_register_decay
algorithms.notes: Invalidates digests after 256 decoded instructions to prevent stale values from poisoning predictions.

algorithms.name: predict_sr
algorithms.trigger: Branch predictor lookup time at fetch
algorithms.notes: Bank scale x2.5 vs x0 is driven per bank by best_usefulness > 0 (resolving U2 as assumed default). Scaled sum sR is passed to the SC summation stage for LSUM calculation.

algorithms.name: update_sr
algorithms.trigger: Branch retirement / commit time (when branch outcome is resolved)
algorithms.pseudocode:
function update_sr(pc: uint64, actual_taken: bool, sc_mispredicted: bool, lsum: int, update_threshold: int, valid_regs_at_pred: array of lists of int):
    // SC update condition: misprediction or low confidence (|lsum| <= update_threshold)
    if not (sc_mispredicted or abs(lsum) <= update_threshold):
        return

    for bank from 0 to 7:
        valid_regs = valid_regs_at_pred[bank]
        if valid_regs is empty:
            continue

        // Single write-port per bank: if multiple registers available, select one randomly
        upd_reg = valid_regs[random() % length(valid_regs)]
        reg_pos = upd_reg // 8

        // Update Usefulness Tables (UT)
        idx_ut0 = hash(pc, 0, bank) % 8
        idx_ut1 = hash(pc, 1, bank) % 8
        idx_ut2 = hash(pc, 2, bank) % 8

        digest = RTT[upd_reg].payload & 0x0FFF
        idx_wt0 = hash(pc, digest, 0, bank) % 512
        idx_wt1 = hash(pc, digest, 1, bank) % 256
        idx_wt2 = hash(pc, digest, 2, bank) % 128

        pred_wt = WT0[bank][idx_wt0] + WT1[bank][idx_wt1] + WT2[bank][idx_wt2]
        reg_correct = (pred_wt >= 0) == actual_taken

        // Reward usefulness if register prediction matched outcome, else penalize
        u_delta = +1 if reg_correct else -1
        UT0[bank][idx_ut0].weights[reg_pos] = sat_add(UT0[bank][idx_ut0].weights[reg_pos], u_delta, -32, 31)
        UT1[bank][idx_ut1].weights[reg_pos] = sat_add(UT1[bank][idx_ut1].weights[reg_pos], u_delta, -32, 31)
        UT2[bank][idx_ut2].weights[reg_pos] = sat_add(UT2[bank][idx_ut2].weights[reg_pos], u_delta, -32, 31)

        // Update Weight Tables (WT)
        wt_delta = +1 if actual_taken else -1
        WT0[bank][idx_wt0] = sat_add(WT0[bank][idx_wt0], wt_delta, -32, 31)
        WT1[bank][idx_wt1] = sat_add(WT1[bank][idx_wt1], wt_delta, -32, 31)
        WT2[bank][idx_wt2] = sat_add(WT2[bank][idx_wt2], wt_delta, -32, 31)
algorithms.notes: Weights and usefulness counters are 6-bit signed values saturated at [-32, 31]. Random register selection per bank guarantees a single write port per bank.

algorithms.name: recover_on_squash
algorithms.notes: Restores pending status on squash. Valid completed digests remain intact, allowing post-flush predictions to leverage completed values.

host_interfaces.need: Logical register write notification at instruction decode
host_interfaces.description: Host notifies predictor at decode of instructions that write an architectural register, supplying logical destination register ID and in-flight ROB tag.
host_interfaces.fallback: If ROB tags are unavailable at decode, assign an internal sequence counter to each pending destination register and match it upon completion.

host_interfaces.need: Register execution result notification at writeback/completion
host_interfaces.description: Host notifies predictor when a register-producing instruction completes execution, providing logical register ID, 64-bit value, register type (INT, FP, FLAG), and associated ROB tag.
host_interfaces.fallback: If 64-bit values cannot be forwarded at execution, forward values at instruction retirement / commit (with reduced post-flush benefit).

host_interfaces.description: Host signals number of instructions decoded each cycle to decrement RTT decay counters (invalidating entries after 256 instructions).
host_interfaces.fallback: Approximate decay using elapsed processor cycles or retired instruction counts.

host_interfaces.need: Pipeline squash / flush notification with flushed instruction tags
host_interfaces.description: Host provides set or range of flushed ROB tags when a mispredicted branch redirects fetch, allowing RTT to invalidate stale pending reservations.
host_interfaces.fallback: Invalidate all pending entries (where valid == 0) upon any pipeline squash.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: WT (Prediction Weight Tables): 6 bits * (512 + 256 + 128) entries * 8 banks = 43,008 bits. UT (Usefulness Weight Tables): 6 bits * 65 registers * (8 + 8 + 8) entries = 9,360 bits. Auxiliary data (RTT): 65 registers * [valid (1) + payload (14) + decay_ctr (8)] = 65 * 23 = 1,495 bits. Total = 43,008 + 9,360 + 1,495 = 53,863 bits (6.57 KiB).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Requires 8 parallel 8-way/9-way comparator trees (one per bank) to find the most useful register, 8 3-input integer adders for UT sum, 8 3-input integer adders for WT sum, fixed-point x2.5 multiplier (shift-and-add: (x << 1) + (x >> 1)), 8-input adder tree for sR, and XOR digest generation circuits.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: At iso-storage, sR storage (6.57 KiB) can be compensated by reducing TAGE high-bank tagged table capacities (e.g. reducing 25 high banks from 2K entries to 1.75K entries or shrinking the 128K bimodal table to 64K entries, saving 10 KiB).

parameters.name: num_banks
parameters.storage_impact: Multiplies total WT capacity and divides register group size proportionally

parameters.name: weight_bits
parameters.storage_impact: Linearly scales storage of WT and UT tables

parameters.name: decay_threshold_insts
parameters.storage_impact: Requires ceil(log2(decay_threshold_insts)) bits per RTT entry

parameters.name: usefulness_scale_factor
parameters.storage_impact: No storage impact (affects ALU scaling logic)

unit_tests.name: int_digest_generation_zeros
unit_tests.expect: Value LSB=0, trailing zeros count=63 (capped), leading zeros count=63 (capped). Digest = (63 & 0x3F) ^ ((63 & 0x3F) << 3) ^ ((0 & 0x3F) << 6) = 0x3F ^ 0x1F8 ^ 0 = 0x1C7 (455)

unit_tests.name: int_digest_generation_powers_of_two
unit_tests.expect: Value LSB = 8 & 0x3F = 8. Trailing zeros = 3. Leading zeros = 60. Digest = (3 & 0x3F) ^ ((60 & 0x3F) << 3) ^ ((8 & 0x3F) << 6) = 3 ^ 0x1E0 ^ 0x200 = 0x3E3 (995)

unit_tests.name: flag_digest_generation
unit_tests.given: A FLAG register with condition-code bits 0b1011 (11)

unit_tests.name: fp32_digest_generation
unit_tests.given: An FP32 register with value 0x40490FDB (approx +3.14159: sign=0, exp=0x80 = 0b10000000). Bits [31:26] = 0b010000 (16)
unit_tests.expect: Digest extracted from Val[31:26] placed at digest[8:3]: (16 << 3) = 128 (0x080), with digest[2:0]=0

unit_tests.name: rtt_expiration_after_256_instructions
unit_tests.given: A completed write to R5 with valid digest at decode cycle 0, followed by 256 consecutive decoded instructions without new writes to R5
unit_tests.expect: At instruction count 255, RTT[5].valid == 1 and decay_ctr == 1. At instruction count 256, RTT[5].valid == 0 and R5 does not participate in branch prediction

unit_tests.name: usefulness_based_bank_gating
unit_tests.given: Bank 0 has valid digest for R0. UT0, UT1, UT2 for R0 sum to -2 (non-positive usefulness). Bank WT0+WT1+WT2 sum to +15
unit_tests.expect: Because best_usefulness <= 0, the bank multiplier selects x0; Bank 0 contributes exactly 0 to sR

unit_tests.name: useful_bank_scaling
unit_tests.given: Bank 1 has valid digest for R1. UT0+UT1+UT2 sum to +4 (positive usefulness). Bank WT0+WT1+WT2 sum to +10
unit_tests.expect: Because best_usefulness > 0, the bank multiplier selects x2.5; Bank 1 contributes int(10 * 2.5) = +25 to sR

unit_tests.name: random_single_update_per_bank
unit_tests.given: Bank 0 had two valid registers at prediction time (R0 and R8). A misprediction occurs triggering an SC update
unit_tests.expect: Exactly one of R0 or R8 is randomly chosen and updated in Bank 0's UT and WT tables, maintaining single write-port constraint per bank

open_questions: U2: The paper (Figure 5(c)) does not label the wire selecting x0 vs x2.5 in each bank. Assumed default: each bank's own usefulness value (> 0 vs <= 0) gates the multiplier (x2.5 when positive, x0 otherwise). Alternative reading: a global static scale of 2.5 is used, or the TAGE hit-bank usefulness drives it.

U3: In Figure 6(a), leading/trailing counts are 6 bits wide for 64-bit registers (which can have up to 64 identical bits). Assumed default: the count saturates at 63. Also, the phrase 'leading zeros (or ones)' does not define how zero/one is distinguished; assumed default counts bits matching the MSB (or LSB), capping naturally at 63.

U4: In Figure 6(b), right alignment of FP fields at digest bit 3 is inferred from Figure 6(b) diagram and edge labels, leaving digest[2:0] unused. Alternative reading: each format is right-aligned at bit 0. Furthermore, format classification logic between FP16, FP32, and FP64 is unspecified; assumed default inspects operand type annotations from host instruction metadata.

Post-misprediction recovery: The paper states that Tomasulo-like table recovery after branch misprediction presents implementation challenges and is left for future work. Assumed default: RTT invalidates pending entries matching flushed ROB tags on a pipeline squash, while keeping already-completed valid digests intact to boost post-flush prediction accuracy.
